question: Which of the following correctly pairs a B-complex vitamin deficiency with its clinical syndrome?

answers.text: Riboflavin (B2) deficiency — pellagra (the 4 Ds: dermatitis, diarrhoea, dementia, death)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Pellagra is caused by Niacin (B3) deficiency, not riboflavin. Riboflavin deficiency causes angular cheilitis, glossitis, seborrhoeic dermatitis, and corneal vascularisation.

answers.text: Thiamine (B1) deficiency — wet beriberi (congestive cardiac failure) in infants of thiamine-deficient mothers

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Thiamine (B1) deficiency causes beriberi: wet beriberi presents with high-output cardiac failure (tachycardia, cardiomegaly, cardiac beriberi) and is the most feared presentation in exclusively breastfed infants of thiamine-deficient mothers.

Incorrect. Megaloblastic anaemia is caused by Folate (B9) or Cobalamin (B12) deficiency, both of which impair DNA synthesis. Pyridoxine (B6) deficiency causes microcytic/sideroblastic anaemia, peripheral neuropathy, and seizures in neonates.

answers.text: Cobalamin (B12) deficiency — wet beriberi with peripheral oedema

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Cobalamin (B12) deficiency causes megaloblastic anaemia and subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord (posterior and lateral column degeneration), not beriberi.

overallFeedback.feedback: Thiamine (B1) deficiency causes beriberi. Niacin (B3) deficiency causes pellagra. Folate/B12 deficiency causes megaloblastic anaemia. Pyridoxine (B6) deficiency causes sideroblastic anaemia and neonatal seizures.
Correct. Thiamine deficiency → beriberi (wet = cardiac; dry = neuropathy; infantile = cardiac beriberi in breastfed infants of deficient mothers).
